benchmark.markdown:
Measured on 1 CPU core(s) with the offline `rules` extractor and hash embedder, so these numbers are the pipeline only; with Gemini enabled add one API call per invoice (latency and quota are the limit, see `LLM_CONCURRENCY`):

| Test | Pages | Invoices found (one per page expected) | Total time | Throughput | Peak memory of the process |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Digital PDF (6.2 MB) | 1000 | 1000 of 1000 | 5.8 s | 172.0 pages/s | 254 MB |
| Scanned PDF (OCR) | 20 | 18 of 20 | 29.3 s | 1.47 s/page | - |

Per-stage time for the large PDF (ms): parse 645, extract 669, validate 3835, index 643, pipeline 5801.
Search index: 400 chunks embedded (text chunks are capped per document; keyword search always covers the full text).
On the scanned PDF 2 page(s) were merged into the previous invoice: the OCR did not read their invoice number clearly enough to start a new invoice (the splitter is conservative on purpose). These documents are flagged for review.
OCR cost is linear in pages: a 1000-page fully scanned PDF would take about 24 min on this machine with 2 OCR thread(s) (**estimate** extrapolated from the measured 1.47 s/page; it divides by the number of worker containers x OCR threads).
